title: Neural networks and fuzzy logic
lead: Choose a question, understand the model, then work the calculation.

title: Neurons, activations and network foundations
lead: A neuron is a weighted sum followed by an activation. Learning changes its weights and bias.

title: Threshold logic and perceptron learning
lead: A perceptron learns a straight decision boundary. Check the label and zero-threshold convention before updating.

title: ADALINE and MADALINE learning
lead: ADALINE learns from its linear response. MADALINE must also decide which hidden units to change.

title: Widrow-Hoff derivation and LMS calculations
lead: Derive the LMS update, keep the factor of two straight, and follow one complete numerical training trace.

title: Multilayer networks and backpropagation
lead: Send activations forward, send error signals backward, then update all parameters from the same old state.

title: Backpropagation variations and deeper networks
lead: Compare momentum, batch learning, adaptive rates and gain changes by what each one actually changes.

title: Probabilistic neural networks
lead: A PNN stores examples, turns distance into Gaussian responses, and averages those responses within each class.

title: Crisp and fuzzy sets
lead: Membership is a degree of fit. With the standard operators, union takes max, intersection takes min, and complement takes 1−μ.

title: Relations and matrix composition
lead: A relation matrix gives grades to ordered pairs. Composition compares routes through a shared middle universe.

title: Membership, fuzzification and defuzzification
lead: Fuzzification gives grades. A cut gives a crisp set. Scalar defuzzification gives one number.

title: Classical logic and crisp rule relations
lead: An implication is false only when its premise is true and its conclusion is false. Use that row to check the rule.

title: Fuzzy propositions, linguistic variables and implications
lead: Translate words into grades, keep the universes separate, and name the implication operator before calculating.

title: Mamdani, Sugeno, Tsukamoto and ANFIS
lead: Mamdani, Sugeno and Tsukamoto share fuzzy rule firing. Their consequent types determine how the final number is calculated.
